  "text": "The constable swore softly beside Ada. At the top of the stairs, his voice swore back, a heartbeat later.

“Keep your hands off the walls,” Venn whispered.

Mara found Ada’s wrist in the dark. The key was cold again. “The date,” she said. “What happens tomorrow?”

A match flared. Elias held it above the ledger, whose cover had begun to buckle. From beneath it came a slow, patient scratching.

Ada turned the blackened paper toward the flame. The date was still there, but another line had appeared below it, written in a cramped hand: AT FIRST LIGHT.

Upstairs, the kitchen door opened. A second set of boots crossed the floor. Then a third.

“We can’t stay here,” the constable said.

“No,” said Venn. He looked at Ada. “You gave it a name. Now it knows it can be named.”

The match burned Elias’s fingers. He dropped it, and as the flame fell, Ada glimpsed a narrow seam in the cellar wall. The stone on either side was wet, though the rest of the cellar was dry.

She pressed the key into Mara’s palm. “Try that.”

Mara fitted its tip into the seam. Stone shifted with a sound like someone drawing a breath. Beyond it lay a passage barely wide enough for one person.

The laughter stopped.

From upstairs, in Ada’s own voice, came a warning: “Don’t go in there.”

Ada looked at the open passage. Fresh bootprints led through it, away from the cellar. She recognized the worn heel of the constable’s left boot."
